Pipkin classification of femoral head fractures

YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

Definition

4 grade system that is used to classify femoral head fractures associated with posterior hip dislocations

Divides the Thompson-Epstein’s Grade 5 (femoral head fracture in association with posterior dislocation) of the hip into four subtypes

  • The classification based on the location of the femoral head fracture
  • These injuries occur after severe high impact trauma such as motor vehicle collisions
  • YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

Grade 1

Small fracture

Inferior to fovea capitis

Not involving the weight bearing surface

YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

Grade 2

Large fracture

Extending superior to the fovea capitis and usually including the fovea

Involving the weightbearing surface

YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

Grade 3

Any femoral head fracture associated with femoral neck fracture

Increased risk of avascular necrosis

YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

Grade 4

Any femoral head fracture associated with acetabular fracture

YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden
